title: Why websites load fast: a copy is usually nearby
description: A CDN keeps copies of site files on servers close to you, which cuts the distance data has to travel.

scenes.sub: a copy of it is probably nearby
scenes.say: Why does a website hosted on another continent load so quickly? Often, you aren't talking to that server at all.

steps: Nearby edge server checks its cache
Cached copy? It replies right away
Otherwise it asks the origin server
scenes.say: You're talking to a CDN, a content delivery network. It's a geographically spread group of servers that cache content close to users. If the nearby server has a copy, it answers instantly.
The origin still holds the real content, but fewer requests reach it. That saves bandwidth, and eases the strain when traffic spikes. It also helps keep a site up if something fails.

lines: edge hit: serves in one hop
scenes.say: Distance is the whole point. Shorter trips mean less delay, and less delay means a faster page. Popular files get cached again and again. Follow for more on how the web works.
